title: Dispositions allowed if not efficient or meritorious causes
source_text: LII. Nam caeteroquin non inviti concedunt ante ipsam justificationem, sensu forensi sumptam, seu quod idem est, ante peccatorum remissionem, in homine multa prae-requiri, quae facile patiuntur vocari dispositiones: modo ne putentur esse justifica-tionis causae efficientes, vel meritoriae. Qualia sunt ea quae jam saepius memoravimus, peccati, scilicet, sensus, agnitio, & detestatio, timor judicii divini, gratiae divinae desiderium & spes, aliqua Dei dilectio, & quae sunt hujusmodi. Ad quae respiciens Petrus, Act. 3. 19. sic Judaeos hortatur, Poenitemini & convertimini, ut deleantur peccata vestra.
pass_a_gloss: For otherwise they not unwillingly concede that before justification itself, taken in the forensic sense, or what is the same, before the remission of sins, many things are prerequisite in a man which they easily allow to be called dispositions—provided they are not thought to be efficient or meritorious causes of justification. Such are those which we have already often mentioned: namely, the sense, acknowledgment, and detestation of sin, fear of divine judgment, desire and hope of divine grace, some love of God, and things of this kind. Looking to which Peter in Acts 3:19 thus exhorts the Jews: Repent and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.
pass_b_english: Otherwise they gladly allow many prerequisites before forensic justification/remission, call them dispositions if not efficient or meritorious causes.
Sense, acknowledgment, detestation of sin, fear, desire and hope of grace, some love—Acts 3:19.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1086.
